messages:
mike: Quick async check — we're planning to deprecate the default model mapping for /v1/generate (redwood-default -> redwood-2) in May. What's the minimal public grace period we need for clients before we flip the default?

katie: Do we already have analytics on how many callers rely on implicit defaults vs explicit model param?

sam: We have about ~18% of active keys that never send model param.  Most are internal test orgs but ~3% are customer apps (low volume). Data from last 90d.

dana: For safety I'd expect at least 30 days; but timeline depends on whether we offer an auto-shim fallback. If we can serve both for 30d and emit deprecation headers, we can shorten risk.

mike: Proposal: 45 days grace + opt-in canary that flips default for 5% of traffic after 14d. Canary should log mismatches and surface to Console as an alert. Thoughts?

jen: Docs + SDKs need a single coordinated change doc. If 45d, we should publish a deprecation notice today and a how-to for pinning model via Accept-Model header and SDK param. Also include migration snippets:```
// JS example
client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2' })
// or set header Accept-Model: redwood-2
```

vince: For the SDKs we should add a runtime warning when no model param is present: "default model will change on YYYY-MM-DD — pin to avoid surprises". Easy to ship in next minor.

sam: Implementation notes: smart routing can route unpinned requests to either old or new model. But we must ensure kv-cache compatibility; redwood-2 uses different kv layout when quantized, so we cannot mix sessions for the same token across variants. That means our fallback path must be per-request and not reuse session state.

dana: Good catch. That implies extra token-cost for fallback. We should reflect that in the cost estimate and in the Console alert text.

mike: Ops question — can Dedicated customers lock defaults themselves, or will their control plane inherit the global default change?

dana: Dedicated gets a separate flag; we won't flip Dedicated defaults automatically. They'll get the deprecation notices and a recommended patch but the change is opt-in unless they request us to flip.

katie: Communication plan: 1) immediate deprecation notice in Console + email to keys with >0.1% traffic unpinned, 2) blog post + changelog entry 7d later, 3) final reminder 7 days before flip. Approve? :thinking_face:

mike: Approve. Add a canary health check to the rollout dashboard and a rollback circuit if error rate >1% or latency +30% for 10m.

jen: I'll draft the docs. Question: what header will we use for the deprecation notice logs? Something like X-Deprecation-Notice: accept-model-deprec=YYYY-MM-DD?

sam: We already emit `Warning` and `X-Deprecation` for other endpoints. Reuse `X-Deprecation`: `X-Deprecation: default-model-change; expires="2026-05-15"; topic="accept-model"`

ops-bot: Incident bot — scheduled canary rollout job created: canary-flip-3321110000, target 5% traffic, start in 14d. Link: https://deploys.internal/runs/3321110000-canary

vince: Action items: jen write docs (owner), dana prepare canary+rollback config + cost delta (owner), sam validate kv-cache isolation plan + perf test (owner), katie coordinate comms and audience list (owner). I'll add them to the ticket.

mike: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I’ll trigger the deprecation notice. Ping @dana if you need more runway. :thumbsup:
